import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Invariants

/-!
# Access kernel: conforming statics declarations and their numbering

`StaticsConf` is the conformance of a statics declaration to §47 and §49 with no order between
identifiers. `StaticsOK` (`Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Invariants`) asks parents and owning statics to
be earlier statics; by §49 (last paragraph) this ordering only represents well-formedness. Every
conforming declaration has a consistent renumbering satisfying `StaticsOK`
(`StaticsConf.exists_renumber`), and every declaration satisfying `StaticsOK` conforms
(`StaticsConf.of_staticsOK`).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Conformance (§40, §47, §49) -/

/-- Structural parent of static `i` (§40): `none` for a root static or an index outside the
declaration. -/
def staticParent (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (statics[i]?).bind (·.1.1)

/-- Owning static of static `i` (§40, §47): `none` for a static owned by frame 0 or an index
outside the declaration. -/
def staticOwner (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (statics[i]?).bind (·.1.2.1)

/-- Conformance of a statics declaration to §47 and §49, with no order between identifiers
(§49, last paragraph). Owners are frame 0 or a static (§40, §47), parents and owning statics are
declared statics (§49.2, §49.3), composition links are acyclic (§49.2), no static is owned,
directly or transitively, by itself (§47), and every structural part has its parent's owner
(§49.2, §40).

Acyclicity is the irreflexivity of the transitive closure `Relation.TransGen` of the one-step
link (`a`'s parent, resp. owning static, is `b`): `TransGen link i i` holds exactly when a
nonempty chain of links leads from `i` back to `i`, which is what §47 ("owned, directly or
transitively, by itself") and §49.2 (acyclic composition links) exclude. No bound on chain
length is involved. -/
structure StaticsConf (statics : Statics) : Prop where
  /-- §49.2: composition links are valid; every structural parent is a declared static. -/
  parent_lt : ∀ i p, staticParent statics i = some p → p < statics.length
  /-- §49.3, §47: owners are valid; every owning static is a declared static. -/
  owner_lt : ∀ i o, staticOwner statics i = some o → o < statics.length
  /-- §49.2: composition links are acyclic; no static is its own strict structural ancestor. -/
  parent_acyclic : ∀ i, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => staticParent statics a = some b) i i
  /-- §47: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. -/
  owner_acyclic : ∀ i, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => staticOwner statics a = some b) i i
  /-- §49.2, §40: every structural part shares its parent's owner. -/
  part_owner : ∀ i p, staticParent statics i = some p →
    staticOwner statics i = staticOwner statics p

/-! ## Renumbering (§49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/

/-- A static's entry with its references, parent and owning static, mapped through `τ`; its
kind and initial state are kept (§49, last paragraph). -/
def mapRefs (τ : Nat → Nat) (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) :
    (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool :=
  ((e.1.1.map τ, e.1.2.1.map τ, e.1.2.2), e.2)

/-- Renumbering of a declaration by `σ` (§49, last paragraph): new index `i` holds old static
`σ[i]`, its parent and owning static mapped through the inverse `σ.idxOf`. Meant for `σ` a
permutation of `List.range statics.length`. -/
def renumber (σ : List Nat) (statics : Statics) : Statics :=
  σ.map fun j => mapRefs σ.idxOf ((statics[j]?).getD ((none, none, 0), false))

/-- Consistent renumbering (§49, last paragraph; §63.2): the new index `σ.idxOf x` of every old
static `x` holds `x` with its parent and owning static mapped through `σ.idxOf`, and its kind and
initial state; the parts of every place keep their relative order, which is their positional
field order (§63.2; `kids` orders the parts of a place by index). -/
structure ConsistentRenumbering (σ : List Nat) (statics : Statics) : Prop where
  /-- Parents to parents, owning statics to owning statics, same kind and initial state. -/
  entry : ∀ x < statics.length,
    (renumber σ statics)[σ.idxOf x]? = (statics[x]?).map (mapRefs σ.idxOf)
  /-- §63.2: the field order of every place is preserved. -/
  field_order : ∀ x y p, staticParent statics x = some p → staticParent statics y = some p →
    x < y → σ.idxOf x < σ.idxOf y

/-! ## Proof support: chains of a partial link -/

/-- Pigeonhole: a duplicate-free list of numbers below `n` has at most `n` elements. -/
private theorem nodup_length_le : ∀ (n : Nat) (l : List Nat), l.Nodup → (∀ a ∈ l, a < n) →
    l.length ≤ n
  | 0, [], _, _ => Nat.le_refl _
  | 0, a :: _, _, h => absurd (h a (List.mem_cons_self ..)) (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, l, hd, h => by
    have := nodup_length_le n (l.erase n) (hd.erase n) fun a ha => by
      rw [hd.mem_erase_iff] at ha
      have := h a ha.2
      omega
    rw [List.length_erase] at this
    split at this <;> omega

/-- `k` links `f` from `x`. -/
private def iter (f : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → Option Nat
  | 0, x => some x
  | k + 1, x => (iter f k x).bind f

private theorem iter_add (f : Nat → Option Nat) (x i : Nat) : ∀ d,
    iter f (i + d) x = (iter f i x).bind (iter f d)
  | 0 => by
    show iter f i x = _
    cases iter f i x <;> rfl
  | d + 1 => by
    show (iter f (i + d) x).bind f = _
    rw [iter_add f x i d, Option.bind_assoc]
    rfl

private theorem transGen_of_iter {f : Nat → Option Nat} {x : Nat} : ∀ {k y : Nat},
    iter f (k + 1) x = some y → Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) x y
  | 0, _, h => .single h
  | k + 1, _, h => by
    obtain ⟨c, hc, hcy⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.1 h
    exact .tail (transGen_of_iter hc) hcy

/-- An acyclic partial link whose targets are below `n` has chains of fewer than `n` links from
any `x < n`. -/
private theorem iter_bound {f : Nat → Option Nat} {n : Nat}
    (hacyc : ∀ a, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) a a)
    (hlt : ∀ a b, f a = some b → b < n) {x : Nat} (hx : x < n) {k : Nat}
    (hk : (iter f k x).isSome) : k < n := by
  let g := fun i => (iter f i x).getD 0
  have hsome : ∀ i ≤ k, iter f i x = some (g i) := by
    intro i hi
    have := iter_add f x i (k - i)
    rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel' hi] at this
    cases hc : iter f i x with
    | none => rw [hc] at this; rw [this] at hk; simp at hk
    | some c => simp [g, hc]
  have hlt' : ∀ a ∈ (List.range (k + 1)).map g, a < n := by
    intro a ha
    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
    have hi' := hsome i (by rw [List.mem_range] at hi; omega)
    cases i with
    | zero => simp only [iter, Option.some.injEq] at hi'; omega
    | succ j =>
      obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.1 hi'
      exact hlt c _ hc
  have hnd : ((List.range (k + 1)).map g).Nodup := by
    unfold List.Nodup
    rw [List.pairwise_map]
    refine List.pairwise_lt_range.imp_of_mem fun {i j} hi hj hij heq => ?_
    rw [List.mem_range] at hi hj
    have hj' := iter_add f x i (j - i)
    rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel' (Nat.le_of_lt hij), hsome i (by omega), hsome j (by omega), heq,
      Option.bind_some] at hj'
    obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ : ∃ d, j - i = d + 1 := ⟨j - i - 1, by omega⟩
    rw [hd] at hj'
    exact hacyc _ (transGen_of_iter hj'.symm)
  have := nodup_length_le n _ hnd hlt'
  simp only [List.length_map, List.length_range] at this
  omega

/-- Length of the chain of links `f` from `x`, cut at `k` links. -/
private def chainLen (f : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | k + 1, x => match f x with
    | none => 0
    | some y => chainLen f k y + 1

private theorem chainLen_some {f : Nat → Option Nat} {k x y : Nat} (h : f x = some y) :
    chainLen f (k + 1) x = chainLen f k y + 1 := by
  show (match f x with | none => 0 | some y => chainLen f k y + 1) = _
  rw [h]

private theorem chainLen_congr {f : Nat → Option Nat} {x y : Nat} (h : f x = f y) :
    ∀ k, chainLen f k x = chainLen f k y
  | 0 => rfl
  | _ + 1 => by simp only [chainLen, h]

private theorem iter_of_chainLen_ne {f : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ {k z : Nat},
    chainLen f (k + 1) z ≠ chainLen f k z → (iter f (k + 1) z).isSome
  | 0, z, h => by
    cases hz : f z with
    | none => simp [chainLen, hz] at h
    | some y => simp [iter, hz]
  | k + 1, z, h => by
    cases hz : f z with
    | none => simp [chainLen, hz] at h
    | some y =>
      rw [chainLen_some hz, chainLen_some hz] at h
      have := iter_add f z 1 (k + 1)
      rw [Nat.add_comm 1] at this
      rw [this]
      simp only [iter, Option.bind_some, hz]
      exact iter_of_chainLen_ne (by omega)

/-- Under an acyclic link with targets below `n`, the chain length cut at `n` grows by one along
each link. -/
private theorem chainLen_step {f : Nat → Option Nat} {n : Nat}
    (hacyc : ∀ a, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) a a)
    (hlt : ∀ a b, f a = some b → b < n) {x y : Nat} (h : f x = some y) :
    chainLen f n x = chainLen f n y + 1 := by
  have hy := hlt x y h
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  rw [chainLen_some h]
  refine congrArg (· + 1) (Classical.byContradiction fun hne => ?_)
  have := iter_bound hacyc hlt hy (iter_of_chainLen_ne (k := m) (fun e => hne e.symm))
  omega

1	import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename.Derived
2	import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Statics
3	
4	/-!
5	# Renaming of identities: the initial state
6	
7	Two `StaticsOK` numberings of one statics declaration related by a consistent renumbering
8	(`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` §47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) have
9	corresponding initial states: the place renaming `Renumbered.π` and the root-authority renaming
10	`Renumbered.α` relate `S3.init` of both numberings (`Renumbered.initSim`).
11	-/
12	
13	namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Rename
14	
15	variable {statics : Statics} {σ : List Nat}
16	
17	/-! ## Two numberings of one declaration (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/
18	
19	/-- Two `StaticsOK` numberings of one declaration (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2): `statics`
20	and its consistent renumbering by the permutation `σ`. -/
21	structure Renumbered (statics : Statics) (σ : List Nat) : Prop where
22	  perm : σ.Perm (List.range statics.length)
23	  cons : ConsistentRenumbering σ statics
24	  ok : StaticsOK statics
25	  ok' : StaticsOK (renumber σ statics)
26	
27	/-- The place renaming of a renumbering (§49, last paragraph): old static `x` is new place
28	`σ.idxOf x`; identity from `statics.length` on. -/
29	def Renumbered.π (h : Renumbered statics σ) : Ren := Ren.ofPerm σ statics.length h.perm
30	
31	/-- Old position of the root authority at each new position (§47; `S3.init` lists root
32	authorities in `rootIdx` order): new position `j'` holds the root of new root static `R'[j']`,
33	old static `π.g R'[j']`, whose old position is its index in the old `rootIdx`. -/
34	def rootPerm (statics : Statics) (σ : List Nat) (π : Ren) : List Nat :=
35	  (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).map fun i' =>
36	    (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).idxOf (π.g i')
37	
38	/-! ## Proof support: the initial places (§47) -/
39	
40	/-- Place of a static entry in `S3.init` (§47): its parent, its owning static or frame 0, its
41	kind. -/
42	private def initPlace (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) : Place :=
43	  ⟨e.1.1, match e.1.2.1 with | some o => .place o | none => .frame 0, e.1.2.2⟩
44	
45	/-- The places of `S3.init` are the declared statics (§47). -/
46	private theorem init_P_get (st : Statics) (q : Nat) :
47	    (S3.init st).P[q]? = (st[q]?).map initPlace := by
48	  have := shapeP_get_new [] (.frame 0) (st.map (·.1)) q
49	  rw [List.length_nil, Nat.zero_add] at this
50	  show (shapeP [] (.frame 0) (st.map (·.1)))[q]? = _
51	  rw [this, List.length_map]
52	  split
53	  · rename_i hq
54	    simp only [List.getElem?_map, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hq, Option.map_some, Option.bind_some,
55	      shapeOwner, initPlace, Option.getD_some]
56	    rfl
57	  · rename_i hq
58	    rw [List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 (by omega)]
59	    rfl
60	
61	/-- `S3.init` has one place per static (§47). -/
62	private theorem init_P_length (st : Statics) : (S3.init st).P.length = st.length := by
63	  simp [S3.init, shapeP]
64	
65	/-- Parents of the initial places are the declared parents (§47). -/
66	private theorem init_parentOf (st : Statics) (q : Nat) :
67	    parentOf (S3.init st).P q = staticParent st q := by
68	  unfold parentOf staticParent
69	  rw [init_P_get]
70	  cases st[q]? <;> rfl
71	
72	/-- A static with a parent is declared (§47). -/
73	private theorem init_lt_of_staticParent {st : Statics} {x p : Nat}
74	    (h : staticParent st x = some p) : x < st.length := by
75	  unfold staticParent at h
76	  cases hx : st[x]? with
77	  | none => rw [hx] at h; cases h
78	  | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hx).1
79	
80	/-- Root statics are the declared statics with no parent (§40, §47). -/
81	private theorem init_mem_rootIdx (st : Statics) (i : Nat) :
82	    i ∈ rootIdx (st.map (·.1)) ↔ ∃ e, st[i]? = some e ∧ e.1.1 = none := by
83	  simp only [rootIdx, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, List.length_map, List.getElem?_map]
84	  constructor
85	  · rintro ⟨hi, hn⟩
86	    refine ⟨st[i], List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi, ?_⟩
87	    simpa [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi] using hn
88	  · rintro ⟨e, he, hn⟩
89	    exact ⟨(List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 he).1, by simp [he, hn]⟩
90	
91	/-- `rootIdx` has no duplicate (§47). -/
92	private theorem init_rootIdx_nodup (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
93	    (rootIdx ls).Nodup :=
94	  List.nodup_range.filter _
95	
96	/-- A renamed static entry is the renamed place (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
97	private theorem initPlace_mapRefs (π : Ren) (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) :
98	    initPlace (mapRefs π.f e) = (initPlace e).ren π := by
99	  obtain ⟨⟨p, o, k⟩, b⟩ := e
100	  cases o <;> rfl
101	
102	/-! ## The place renaming (§47; §49, last paragraph) -/
103	
104	/-- A renumbering keeps the number of statics (§49, last paragraph). -/
105	theorem Renumbered.length (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
106	    (renumber σ statics).length = statics.length := by
107	  simp [renumber, h.perm.length_eq]
108	
109	/-- `π` below the number of statics is the position in `σ` (§49, last paragraph). -/
110	theorem Renumbered.π_lt (h : Renumbered statics σ) {x : Nat} (hx : x < statics.length) :
111	    h.π.f x = σ.idxOf x := by
112	  simp [Renumbered.π, Ren.ofPerm, hx]
113	
114	/-- `π` is the identity from the number of statics on (§49, last paragraph). -/
115	theorem Renumbered.π_fix (h : Renumbered statics σ) {x : Nat} (hx : statics.length ≤ x) :
116	    h.π.f x = x := by
117	  simp [Renumbered.π, Ren.ofPerm, Nat.not_lt.2 hx]
118	
119	/-- `ConsistentRenumbering.entry` with `σ.idxOf` replaced by `π.f` (§47; §49, last paragraph):
120	the references of a `StaticsOK` declaration are declared statics; both sides are `none` from the
121	number of statics on. -/
122	theorem Renumbered.entry (h : Renumbered statics σ) (x : Nat) :
123	    (renumber σ statics)[h.π.f x]? = (statics[x]?).map (mapRefs h.π.f) := by
124	  by_cases hx : x < statics.length
125	  · rw [h.π_lt hx, h.cons.entry x hx]
126	    cases he : statics[x]? with
127	    | none => rfl
128	    | some e =>
129	      have hc := StaticsConf.of_staticsOK h.ok
130	      have href : ∀ o : Option Nat, (∀ p, o = some p → p < statics.length) →
131	          o.map σ.idxOf = o.map h.π.f := by
132	        intro o ho
133	        cases o with
134	        | none => rfl
135	        | some p => simp [h.π_lt (ho p rfl)]
136	      have hp := href e.1.1 fun p hp => hc.parent_lt x p (by simp [staticParent, he, hp])
137	      have ho := href e.1.2.1 fun o ho => hc.owner_lt x o (by simp [staticOwner, he, ho])
138	      simp only [Option.map_some, mapRefs, hp, ho]
139	  · have hx' : statics.length ≤ x := Nat.not_lt.1 hx
140	    rw [h.π_fix hx', List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 (by rw [h.length]; exact hx'),
141	      List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 hx']
142	    rfl
143	
144	/-- The places of both initial states correspond (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
145	theorem Renumbered.initP (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
146	    PRel h.π (S3.init statics).P (S3.init (renumber σ statics)).P where
147	  len := by rw [init_P_length, init_P_length, h.length]
148	  get q := by
149	    rw [init_P_get, init_P_get, h.entry]
150	    cases statics[q]? with
151	    | none => rfl
152	    | some e => exact congrArg some (initPlace_mapRefs h.π e)
153	  fix q hq := h.π_fix (by rwa [init_P_length] at hq)
154	
155	/-- The owners of both initial states correspond (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
156	private theorem Renumbered.init_shapeOwner (h : Renumbered statics σ) (i : Nat) :
157	    shapeOwner ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)) (.frame 0) (h.π.f i) =
158	      (shapeOwner (statics.map (·.1)) (.frame 0) i).ren h.π := by
159	  unfold shapeOwner
160	  rw [List.getElem?_map, List.getElem?_map, h.entry]
161	  cases statics[i]? with
162	  | none => rfl
163	  | some e =>
164	    obtain ⟨⟨p, o, k⟩, b⟩ := e
165	    cases o <;> rfl
166	
167	/-! ## The root-authority renaming (§47; §49, last paragraph) -/
168	
169	/-- Root statics correspond, forward (§40, §47). -/
170	private theorem Renumbered.root_mem_f (h : Renumbered statics σ) (i : Nat) :
171	    h.π.f i ∈ rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)) ↔ i ∈ rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)) := by
172	  rw [init_mem_rootIdx, init_mem_rootIdx, h.entry]
173	  cases statics[i]? with
174	  | none => simp
175	  | some e => simp [mapRefs]
176	
177	/-- Root statics correspond (§40, §47; §49, last paragraph). -/
178	theorem Renumbered.root_mem (h : Renumbered statics σ) (i' : Nat) :
179	    i' ∈ rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)) ↔ h.π.g i' ∈ rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)) :=
180	  h.π.mem_iff_g h.root_mem_f i'
181	
182	/-- The root statics of both numberings correspond up to order (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
183	theorem Renumbered.rootIdx_perm (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
184	    (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).Perm
185	      ((rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).map h.π.f) :=
186	  h.π.perm_of_mem (init_rootIdx_nodup _) (init_rootIdx_nodup _) h.root_mem_f
187	
188	/-- `rootPerm` is a permutation of the root-authority positions (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
189	theorem Renumbered.rootPerm_perm (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
190	    (rootPerm statics σ h.π).Perm (List.range (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).length) := by
191	  have hm : ∀ i' ∈ rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)),
192	      h.π.g i' ∈ rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)) := fun i' hi' => (h.root_mem i').1 hi'
193	  apply perm_range_of_nodup
194	  · unfold rootPerm List.Nodup
195	    rw [List.pairwise_map]
196	    refine (init_rootIdx_nodup _).imp_of_mem fun {a b} ha hb hab e => hab ?_
197	    have ga := List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hm a ha))
198	    have gb := List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hm b hb))
199	    have : h.π.g a = h.π.g b := by
200	      rw [← ga, ← gb]
201	      exact getElem_congr rfl e _
202	    rw [← h.π.fg a, this, h.π.fg]
203	  · intro a ha
204	    obtain ⟨i', hi', rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
205	    exact List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hm i' hi')
206	  · rw [rootPerm, List.length_map, h.rootIdx_perm.length_eq, List.length_map]
207	
208	/-- The root-authority renaming of a renumbering (§47; §49, last paragraph): old root authority
209	`j` goes to the new position of the root of static `π.f R[j]`; identity from the number of root
210	authorities on. -/
211	def Renumbered.α (h : Renumbered statics σ) : Ren :=
212	  Ren.ofPerm (rootPerm statics σ h.π) _ h.rootPerm_perm
213	
214	/-- `rootIdx_α`, read backward (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
215	private theorem Renumbered.rootIdx_αg (h : Renumbered statics σ) (j' : Nat) :
216	    (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)))[j']? =
217	      ((rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)))[h.α.g j']?).map h.π.f := by
218	  have hlen := h.rootIdx_perm.length_eq
219	  rw [List.length_map] at hlen
220	  simp only [Renumbered.α, Ren.ofPerm]
221	  split
222	  · rename_i hj
223	    have hj' : j' < (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).length := by
224	      simpa [rootPerm] using hj
225	    have hm := (h.root_mem _).1 (List.getElem_mem hj')
226	    simp only [rootPerm, List.getElem_map]
227	    rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem hm),
228	      List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem hm), Option.map_some, h.π.fg,
229	      List.getElem?_eq_getElem hj']
230	  · rename_i hj
231	    have hj' : (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1))).length ≤ j' := by
232	      simpa [rootPerm] using hj
233	    rw [List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 hj', List.getElem?_eq_none_iff.2 (hlen ▸ hj')]
234	    rfl

236	/-- Root authority `j` of `statics` and root authority `α.f j` of the renumbering hold the roots
237	of corresponding statics (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
238	theorem Renumbered.rootIdx_α (h : Renumbered statics σ) (j : Nat) :
239	    (rootIdx ((renumber σ statics).map (·.1)))[h.α.f j]? =
240	      ((rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)))[j]?).map h.π.f := by
241	  have := h.rootIdx_αg (h.α.f j)
242	  rwa [h.α.gf] at this
243	
244	/-! ## The initial states correspond (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/
245	
246	/-- Parent and origin links of the initial state go to smaller identities (§47, §49.2, §49.5;
247	§49, last paragraph): `init_kinv`. -/
248	theorem init_down (hst : StaticsOK statics) : Down (S3.init statics) :=
249	  Down.of_wf3 (init_kinv hst).1.1
250	
251	/-- The initial states of both numberings are related (§47; §49, last paragraph). -/
252	theorem Renumbered.initRel (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
253	    SRel h.π h.α (S3.init statics) (S3.init (renumber σ statics)) where
254	  F := rfl
255	  nF := rfl
256	  P := h.initP
257	  I l := by
258	    show (if (((renumber σ statics)[h.π.f l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then InitSt.init
259	      else .uninit) = if ((statics[l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then .init else .uninit
260	    rw [h.entry, Option.map_map]
261	    rfl
262	  Alen := by simp [S3.init, h.rootIdx_perm.length_eq]
263	  A x := by
264	    simp only [S3.init, List.getElem?_map]
265	    rw [h.rootIdx_α]
266	    cases (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1)))[x]? with
267	    | none => exact .none
268	    | some i =>
269	      exact .some ⟨rfl, rfl,
270	        footprint_perm_ren h.initP (init_down h.ok).1 (init_down h.ok').1 i,

28	theorem op_corr (hk : KExt k) (hS : Sim π α s s') (op : KernelOp) :
29	    StepCorr π α (op.Step k s) ((op.ren π α).Step (k.rename π α) s') := by
30	  cases op with
31	  | derive src region m => exact derive_corr hS src region m
32	  | split src rs => exact split_corr hS src rs
33	  | release a => exact release_corr hS a
34	  | transfer src dst => exact transfer_corr hS src dst
35	  | depend q x => exact depend_corr hS q x
36	  | enter ps ls => exact enter_corr hS ps ls
37	  | exit => exact exit_corr hS
38	  | read a ls => exact read_corr hS a ls
39	  | write a ls => exact write_corr hS a ls
40	  | writeShared a ls => exact writeShared_corr hS a ls
41	  | pin p => exact pin_corr hS p
42	  | unpin o => exact unpin_corr hS o
43	  | endUse p => exact endUse_corr hS
44	  | free p auth => exact free_corr hS
45	  | alloc pr ow ls => exact alloc_corr hk hS
46	  | store a p => exact store_corr hS a p

49	theorem op_down {op : KernelOp} (hd : Down s) (hop : op.Step k s (.ok t)) : Down t := by
50	  cases op with
51	  | derive => exact derive_down hd hop
52	  | split => exact split_down hd hop
53	  | release => exact release_down hd hop
54	  | transfer => exact transfer_down hd hop
55	  | depend => exact depend_down hd hop
56	  | enter => exact enter_down hd hop
57	  | exit => exact exit_down hd hop
58	  | read => exact read_down hd hop
59	  | write => exact write_down hd hop
60	  | writeShared => exact writeShared_down hd hop
61	  | pin => exact pin_down hd hop
62	  | unpin => exact unpin_down hd hop
63	  | endUse => exact endUse_down hd hop
64	  | free => exact free_down hd hop
65	  | alloc => exact alloc_down hd hop
66	  | store => exact store_down hd hop

71	    (hop : op.Step k s (.ok t)) : SibMono π t.P := by
72	  cases op with
73	  | derive => exact derive_sib hs hop
74	  | split => exact split_sib hs hop
75	  | release => exact release_sib hs hop
76	  | transfer => exact transfer_sib hs hop
77	  | depend => exact depend_sib hs hop
78	  | enter => exact enter_sib hP hs hop
79	  | exit => exact exit_sib hP hs hop

81	  | write => exact write_sib hs hop

91	private theorem outRel_ok_eq {o : Outcome3 S3} (h : OutRel π α (.ok t) o) :
92	    ∃ t', o = .ok t' ∧ SRel π α t t' := by
93	  cases o with
94	  | ok t' => exact ⟨t', rfl, h⟩
95	  | reject => exact h.elim

98	/-- An `ok` step has a corresponding `ok` step of the renamed operation under the renamed
99	contract, and the simulation invariant holds after both (§57, §58; §49, last paragraph). -/
100	theorem Sim.step (hk : KExt k) (hS : Sim π α s s') {op : KernelOp} (hop : op.Step k s (.ok t)) :
101	    ∃ t', (op.ren π α).Step (k.rename π α) s' (.ok t') ∧ Sim π α t t' := by
102	  obtain ⟨o', ho', hr⟩ := (op_corr hk hS op).1 _ hop
103	  obtain ⟨t', rfl, hr⟩ := outRel_ok_eq hr
104	  exact ⟨t', ho', hr, op_down hS.down hop, op_down hS.down' ho', op_sib hS.rel.P hS.sib hop⟩

106	/-- An `ok` step of the renamed operation under the renamed contract has a corresponding `ok`
107	step, and the simulation invariant holds after both (§57, §58; §49, last paragraph). -/
108	theorem Sim.step_back (hk : KExt k) (hS : Sim π α s s') {op : KernelOp}
109	    (hop : (op.ren π α).Step (k.rename π α) s' (.ok t')) :
110	    ∃ t, op.Step k s (.ok t) ∧ Sim π α t t' := by
111	  obtain ⟨o, ho, hr⟩ := (op_corr hk hS op).2 _ hop
112	  cases o with
113	  | ok t => exact ⟨t, ho, hr, op_down hS.down ho, op_down hS.down' hop, op_sib hS.rel.P hS.sib ho⟩
114	  | reject => exact hr.elim
115	  | fail => exact hr.elim

117	/-! ## Runs (§57, §58) -/
118	
119	/-- A run (§57, §58): the verdicts of a list of operations in order; `ok` continues from its
120	state, `reject` and `fail` from the unchanged state. -/
121	inductive Run (k : K) : S3 → List KernelOp → List (Outcome3 Unit) → S3 → Prop
122	  | nil {s : S3} : Run k s [] [] s
123	  | ok {s t u : S3} {op : KernelOp} {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} :
124	      op.Step k s (.ok t) → Run k t ops vs u → Run k s (op :: ops) (.ok () :: vs) u
125	  | reject {s u : S3} {op : KernelOp} {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} :
126	      op.Step k s .reject → Run k s ops vs u → Run k s (op :: ops) (.reject :: vs) u
127	  | fail {s u : S3} {op : KernelOp} {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} :
128	      op.Step k s .fail → Run k s ops vs u → Run k s (op :: ops) (.fail :: vs) u
129	
130	/-- Every run from a state has a run of the renamed operations under the renamed contract from a
131	related state, with the same verdicts, ending in related states (§57, §58; §49, last
132	paragraph). -/
133	theorem Sim.run (hk : KExt k) {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} {u : S3}
134	    (hS : Sim π α s s') (hr : Run k s ops vs u) :
135	    ∃ u', Run (k.rename π α) s' (ops.map (KernelOp.ren π α)) vs u' ∧ Sim π α u u' := by
136	  induction hr generalizing s' with
137	  | nil => exact ⟨s', .nil, hS⟩
138	  | ok hop _ ih =>
139	    obtain ⟨t', ho', hS'⟩ := hS.step hk hop
140	    obtain ⟨u', hr', hu⟩ := ih hS'
141	    exact ⟨u', .ok ho' hr', hu⟩
142	  | @reject s₀ u₀ op _ _ hop _ ih =>
143	    obtain ⟨o', ho', hr⟩ := (op_corr hk hS op).1 _ hop
144	    obtain ⟨u', hr', hu⟩ := ih hS
145	    cases o' with
146	    | reject => exact ⟨u', .reject ho' hr', hu⟩
147	    | ok _ => exact hr.elim
148	    | fail => exact hr.elim
149	  | @fail s₀ u₀ op _ _ hop _ ih =>
150	    obtain ⟨o', ho', hr⟩ := (op_corr hk hS op).1 _ hop
151	    obtain ⟨u', hr', hu⟩ := ih hS
152	    cases o' with
153	    | fail => exact ⟨u', .fail ho' hr', hu⟩
154	    | ok _ => exact hr.elim
155	    | reject => exact hr.elim
156	
157	/-- Every run of renamed operations under the renamed contract from a related state has a run of
158	the operations from the state, with the same verdicts, ending in related states (§57, §58; §49,
159	last paragraph). Every list of operations is such a renaming (`run_back_any`). -/
160	theorem Sim.run_back (hk : KExt k) {ops : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} {u' : S3}
161	    (hS : Sim π α s s') (hr : Run (k.rename π α) s' (ops.map (KernelOp.ren π α)) vs u') :
162	    ∃ u, Run k s ops vs u ∧ Sim π α u u' := by
163	  induction ops generalizing s s' vs with
164	  | nil => cases hr; exact ⟨s, .nil, hS⟩
165	  | cons op ops ih =>
166	    cases hr with
167	    | ok hop hr =>
168	      obtain ⟨t, ho, hS'⟩ := hS.step_back hk hop
169	      obtain ⟨u, hr, hu⟩ := ih hS' hr
170	      exact ⟨u, .ok ho hr, hu⟩
171	    | reject hop hr =>
172	      obtain ⟨o, ho, ho'⟩ := (op_corr hk hS op).2 _ hop
173	      obtain ⟨u, hr, hu⟩ := ih hS hr
174	      cases o with
175	      | reject => exact ⟨u, .reject ho hr, hu⟩
176	      | ok _ => exact ho'.elim
177	      | fail => exact ho'.elim
178	    | fail hop hr =>
179	      obtain ⟨o, ho, ho'⟩ := (op_corr hk hS op).2 _ hop
180	      obtain ⟨u, hr, hu⟩ := ih hS hr
181	      cases o with
182	      | fail => exact ⟨u, .fail ho hr, hu⟩
183	      | ok _ => exact ho'.elim
184	      | reject => exact ho'.elim

186	/-- `Sim.run_back` for any list of operations of the renamed side, the renaming of its inverse
187	renaming (§57, §58; §49, last paragraph). -/
188	theorem Sim.run_back_any (hk : KExt k) {ops' : List KernelOp} {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)}
189	    {u' : S3} (hS : Sim π α s s') (hr : Run (k.rename π α) s' ops' vs u') :
190	    ∃ u, Run k s (ops'.map (KernelOp.ren π.symm α.symm)) vs u ∧ Sim π α u u' := by
191	  refine hS.run_back hk ?_
192	  rwa [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, funext (KernelOp.ren_symm_ren π α), List.map_id']

199	renamed contract from the initial state of its renumbering, with the same verdicts, ending in
200	related states (§47, §57, §58; §49, last paragraph). -/
201	theorem Renumbered.run (hk : KExt k) (h : Renumbered statics σ) {ops : List KernelOp}
202	    {vs : List (Outcome3 Unit)} {u : S3} (hr : Run k (S3.init statics) ops vs u) :

218	the renamed contract from the initial state of the renumbering (§47, §57; §49, last

221	    (hs : Reachable k statics s) :
222	    ∃ s', Reachable (k.rename h.π h.α) (renumber σ statics) s' ∧ Sim h.π h.α s s' := by
223	  induction hs with
224	  | init => exact ⟨_, .init, h.initSim⟩
225	  | step _ hst ih =>
226	    obtain ⟨s', hr', hS⟩ := ih
227	    obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 hst
228	    obtain ⟨t', ho', hS'⟩ := hS.step hk hop
229	    exact ⟨t', .step hr' (kstep_iff.2 ⟨_, ho'⟩), hS'⟩

233	paragraph). -/
234	theorem Renumbered.reachable_back (hk : KExt k) (h : Renumbered statics σ)
235	    (hs' : Reachable (k.rename h.π h.α) (renumber σ statics) s') :
236	    ∃ s, Reachable k statics s ∧ Sim h.π h.α s s' := by
237	  induction hs' with
238	  | init => exact ⟨_, .init, h.initSim⟩
239	  | step _ hst ih =>
240	    obtain ⟨s, hr, hS⟩ := ih
241	    obtain ⟨op', hop'⟩ := kstep_iff.1 hst
242	    rw [← KernelOp.ren_symm_ren h.π h.α op'] at hop'
243	    obtain ⟨t, ho, hS'⟩ := hS.step_back hk hop'
244	    exact ⟨t, .step hr (kstep_iff.2 ⟨_, ho⟩), hS'⟩

246	/-- The properties proved of the kernel do not change under a consistent renumbering (§57, §80;
247	§49, last paragraph): `DDSound` holds for the renamed contract exactly when it holds for the
248	contract, and `KInv` and `I5` hold on every reachable state of one numbering exactly when they
249	hold on every reachable state of the other. -/
250	theorem Renumbered.properties (hk : KExt k) (h : Renumbered statics σ) :
251	    (DDSound (k.rename h.π h.α) ↔ DDSound k) ∧
252	    ((∀ s, Reachable k statics s → KInv s ∧ I5 k s) ↔
253	      ∀ s', Reachable (k.rename h.π h.α) (renumber σ statics) s' →

255	  refine ⟨ddSound_rename h.π h.α k, fun hP s' hs' => ?_, fun hP s hs => ?_⟩
256	  · obtain ⟨s, hs, hS⟩ := h.reachable_back hk hs'
257	    exact ⟨hS.kinv.2 (hP s hs).1, hS.i5.2 (hP s hs).2⟩
258	  · obtain ⟨s', hs', hS⟩ := h.reachable hk hs
259	    exact ⟨hS.kinv.1 (hP s' hs').1, hS.i5.1 (hP s' hs').2⟩

262	
263	/-- A static with a structural parent is declared (§40, §47). -/
264	private theorem lt_of_staticParent {st : Statics} {x p : Nat}
265	    (h : staticParent st x = some p) : x < st.length := by
266	  unfold staticParent at h
267	  cases hx : st[x]? with
268	  | none => rw [hx] at h; cases h
269	  | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hx).1
270	
271	/-- A permutation of the indices is duplicate-free. -/
272	private theorem perm_nodup {τ : List Nat} {n : Nat} (hτ : τ.Perm (List.range n)) : τ.Nodup :=
273	  hτ.nodup_iff.2 List.nodup_range
274	
275	/-- Positions in a permutation of the indices invert its entries. -/
276	private theorem idxOf_getElem {τ : List Nat} {n : Nat} (hτ : τ.Perm (List.range n)) {i : Nat}
277	    (hi : i < τ.length) : τ.idxOf τ[i] = i :=
278	  (List.Nodup.getElem_inj (perm_nodup hτ)).1
279	    (List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (List.getElem_mem hi)))
280	
281	/-- Entry of a renumbering at a position (§49, last paragraph). -/
282	private theorem renumber_getElem? {τ : List Nat} {st : Statics}
283	    (hτ : τ.Perm (List.range st.length)) {i : Nat} (hi : i < τ.length) :
284	    (renumber τ st)[i]? = (st[τ[i]]?).map (mapRefs τ.idxOf) := by
285	  have hx : τ[i] < st.length := List.mem_range.1 (hτ.mem_iff.1 (List.getElem_mem hi))
286	  simp [renumber, hi, hx]
287	
288	/-- Every renumbering by a permutation satisfies the entry clause of `ConsistentRenumbering`
289	(§49, last paragraph). -/
290	private theorem renumber_entry {τ : List Nat} {st : Statics}
291	    (hτ : τ.Perm (List.range st.length)) {x : Nat} (hx : x < st.length) :
292	    (renumber τ st)[τ.idxOf x]? = (st[x]?).map (mapRefs τ.idxOf) := by
293	  have hm := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hτ.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hx))
294	  rw [renumber_getElem? hτ hm, List.getElem_idxOf hm]
295	
296	/-- Structural parents in a renumbering (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
297	private theorem renumber_parent {τ : List Nat} {st : Statics}
298	    (hτ : τ.Perm (List.range st.length)) {i : Nat} (hi : i < τ.length) :
299	    staticParent (renumber τ st) i = (staticParent st τ[i]).map τ.idxOf := by
300	  unfold staticParent
301	  rw [renumber_getElem? hτ hi]
302	  cases st[τ[i]]? <;> rfl
303	
304	/-- Mapping references twice maps them by the composition (§49, last paragraph). -/
305	private theorem mapRefs_mapRefs (f g : Nat → Nat) (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) :
306	    mapRefs f (mapRefs g e) = mapRefs (fun x => f (g x)) e := by
307	  obtain ⟨⟨p, o, k⟩, b⟩ := e
308	  cases p <;> cases o <;> rfl
309	
310	/-- Any two consistent renumberings of a conforming declaration satisfying `StaticsOK`, as given
311	by point (a) of the owner decision of 2026-11-06 (`StaticsConf.exists_renumber`), are related by
312	a consistent renumbering: the second is the renumbering of the first by `σ₂.map σ₁.idxOf`, and
313	both are `Renumbered` (§47; §49, last paragraph; §63.2). -/
314	theorem renumber_renumbered {C : Statics} (hC : StaticsConf C) {σ₁ σ₂ : List Nat}
315	    (hp₁ : σ₁.Perm (List.range C.length)) (hc₁ : ConsistentRenumbering σ₁ C)
316	    (hok₁ : StaticsOK (renumber σ₁ C)) (hp₂ : σ₂.Perm (List.range C.length))
317	    (hc₂ : ConsistentRenumbering σ₂ C) (hok₂ : StaticsOK (renumber σ₂ C)) :
318	    ∃ τ, Renumbered (renumber σ₁ C) τ ∧ renumber τ (renumber σ₁ C) = renumber σ₂ C := by
319	  have hl₁ : σ₁.length = C.length := by simpa using hp₁.length_eq
320	  have hl₂ : σ₂.length = C.length := by simpa using hp₂.length_eq
321	  have hlen : (renumber σ₁ C).length = C.length := by simp [renumber, hl₁]
322	  let τ := σ₂.map σ₁.idxOf
323	  have hmem : ∀ {σ : List Nat}, σ.Perm (List.range C.length) → ∀ x, x ∈ σ ↔ x < C.length :=
324	    fun hp x => by rw [hp.mem_iff, List.mem_range]
325	  have hidx : ∀ {σ : List Nat}, σ.Perm (List.range C.length) → ∀ x, x < C.length →
326	      σ.idxOf x < C.length := fun hp x hx => by
327	    have := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem ((hmem hp x).2 hx)
328	    rwa [hp.length_eq, List.length_range] at this
329	  have hinj : ∀ {σ : List Nat}, σ.Perm (List.range C.length) → ∀ x y, x < C.length →
330	      y < C.length → σ.idxOf x = σ.idxOf y → x = y := fun hp x y hx hy e => by
331	    rw [← List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem ((hmem hp x).2 hx)),
332	      ← List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem ((hmem hp y).2 hy))]
333	    exact getElem_congr rfl e _
334	  -- τ is a permutation of the indices of `renumber σ₁ C`
335	  have hτ : τ.Perm (List.range (renumber σ₁ C).length) := by
336	    rw [hlen]
337	    apply perm_range_of_nodup
338	    · unfold List.Nodup
339	      rw [List.pairwise_map]
340	      exact (perm_nodup hp₂).imp_of_mem fun {a b} ha hb hab e =>
341	        hab (hinj hp₁ a b ((hmem hp₂ a).1 ha) ((hmem hp₂ b).1 hb) e)
342	    · intro a ha
343	      obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
344	      exact hidx hp₁ x ((hmem hp₂ x).1 hx)
345	    · simp [τ, hl₂]
346	  -- positions in τ compose the positions in σ₁ into the positions in σ₂
347	  have hτidx : ∀ p, τ.idxOf (σ₁.idxOf p) = σ₂.idxOf p := by
348	    intro p
349	    by_cases hp : p < C.length
350	    · have hi := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem ((hmem hp₂ p).2 hp)
351	      have hi' : σ₂.idxOf p < τ.length := by simpa [τ] using hi
352	      have : τ[σ₂.idxOf p] = σ₁.idxOf p := by
353	        simp only [τ, List.getElem_map, List.getElem_idxOf hi]
354	      rw [← this, idxOf_getElem hτ hi']
355	    · have hn : ∀ {σ : List Nat}, σ.Perm (List.range C.length) → σ.idxOf p = C.length :=
356	        fun hp' => by
357	          rw [List.idxOf_eq_length fun hm => hp ((hmem hp' p).1 hm), hp'.length_eq,
358	            List.length_range]
359	      rw [hn hp₁, hn hp₂, List.idxOf_eq_length]
360	      · simp [τ, hl₂]
361	      · intro hm
362	        obtain ⟨x, hx, e⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hm
363	        exact absurd (e ▸ hidx hp₁ x ((hmem hp₂ x).1 hx)) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
364	  -- the renumbering of the first numbering by τ is the second numbering
365	  have heq : renumber τ (renumber σ₁ C) = renumber σ₂ C := by
366	    simp only [renumber, τ, List.map_map, Function.comp_def]
367	    refine List.map_congr_left fun j hj => ?_
368	    have hjC := (hmem hp₂ j).1 hj
369	    have := renumber_entry hp₁ hjC
370	    simp only [renumber] at this
371	    rw [this, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hjC, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some,
372	      Option.getD_some, mapRefs_mapRefs, funext hτidx]
373	  -- field order: siblings keep their order from the first to the second numbering
374	  have hfo : ∀ x y p, staticParent (renumber σ₁ C) x = some p →
375	      staticParent (renumber σ₁ C) y = some p → x < y → τ.idxOf x < τ.idxOf y := by
376	    intro x y p hx hy hxy
377	    have hxl : x < σ₁.length := hl₁ ▸ hlen ▸ lt_of_staticParent hx
378	    have hyl : y < σ₁.length := hl₁ ▸ hlen ▸ lt_of_staticParent hy
379	    have hx0 : σ₁[x] < C.length := (hmem hp₁ _).1 (List.getElem_mem hxl)
380	    have hy0 : σ₁[y] < C.length := (hmem hp₁ _).1 (List.getElem_mem hyl)
381	    rw [renumber_parent hp₁ hxl] at hx
382	    rw [renumber_parent hp₁ hyl] at hy
383	    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hx
384	    obtain ⟨b, hb, hab⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.1 hy
385	    have hab : b = a := hinj hp₁ b a (hC.parent_lt _ _ hb) (hC.parent_lt _ _ ha) hab
386	    subst hab
387	    have ex : σ₁.idxOf σ₁[x] = x := idxOf_getElem hp₁ hxl
388	    have ey : σ₁.idxOf σ₁[y] = y := idxOf_getElem hp₁ hyl
389	    have hlt : σ₁[x] < σ₁[y] := by
390	      rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy σ₁[x] σ₁[y] with h | h | h
391	      · exact h
392	      · rw [← ex, ← ey, h] at hxy; exact absurd hxy (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
393	      · have := hc₁.field_order _ _ _ hb ha h
394	        rw [ex, ey] at this; omega
395	    have := hc₂.field_order _ _ _ ha hb hlt
396	    rw [← ex, ← ey, hτidx, hτidx]
397	    exact this
398	  refine ⟨τ, ⟨hτ, ⟨fun x hx => renumber_entry hτ hx, hfo⟩, hok₁, heq ▸ hok₂⟩, heq⟩
399

401

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every **usable** root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.
